# 8 CTV Advertising Examples: What Ran, Where, and What It Delivered

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/plugins/Basic/assets/placeholder.60f9b1840c.svg)

Tatev Malkhasyan

[

](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tatevikmalkhasyan/)

15

min read

Published:

02.03.2026

·

Updated:

October 5, 2026

_Originally published March 2026. Updated and refreshed in October 2026._

Most roundups of connected TV campaigns hand you a composite: an unnamed retailer, an undated result, a percentage floating free of any study. Every campaign on this page comes with a brand, a platform, a year, and a link to whoever measured it.

![5 CTV Advertising Examples: Real-World Campaign Patterns That Drive Results in 2026](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/69a18e5fa71a1769128536f9/6a6c7c9244b5a1d98f297d81_69a53fbe7edaca025426b7df_5%2520CTV%2520Advertising%2520Examples_%2520Real-World%2520Campaign%2520Patterns%2520That%2520Drive%2520Results%2520in%25202026.webp)

Search for **CTV advertising examples** and the same few campaigns keep circulating, usually with the year stripped out and the source three blog posts back. One of the most widely republished results on the topic is from 2018; another describes a brand relaunch that ran across five media channels, only one of which was streaming.

The eight campaigns below ran between 2024 and 2026 on **Roku, The Trade Desk, Samsung, Disney, Hulu, and Reddit**, and every one of them names its brand. Each entry sets out what ran, where it ran, who it targeted, what it delivered, and which company published the number, with a link to the original. The budgets range from a furniture retailer's small trial to a global technology brand buying programmatically across two streamers, and where a figure comes from the platform that sold the media, the entry says so.

## TL;DR: Key takeaways

*   [**Self-serve platforms**](https://www.aidigital.com/blog/self-serve-advertising-platform) **changed who can buy TV.** Four of the eight campaigns ran through interfaces a two-person marketing team can operate, with no agency, no insertion order, and no upfront commitment. A regional dealer group and a wellness startup now buy the same inventory as [national advertisers](https://www.aidigital.com/blog/top-tv-advertisers).
*   **Audience logic decides performance more than budget size does.** The strongest results came from campaigns built on first-party data, retail-media signals, or purchase-intent segments, with past customers suppressed. The weakest CTV buying still starts from available inventory and works backward.
*   **Interactive formats moved from experiment to line item.** Shoppable overlays, pause units, and remote-activated calls to action carried real revenue in five of these campaigns, and agencies now plan them as a fixed share of CTV budgets instead of a quarterly experiment.
*   **Cost per outcome separates the eight from the field.** Cost per unique household, cost per completed view, and cost per page view appear in almost every one. Impression counts and completion rates appear as context, never as the result.

## What is CTV advertising?

**Connected TV advertising** delivers video ads to internet-connected television devices—[smart TVs](https://www.aidigital.com/blog/smart-tv-advertising), streaming sticks, and consoles—instead of routing them through broadcast or cable. What separates the two for an advertiser is the buying model. Linear sells demographics against fixed time slots, while CTV opens up household-level addressability, programmatic execution, and reporting tied to outcomes.

Viewing has followed the hardware. Streaming took 48.6% of total US TV watch-time in May 2026, [](https://www.nielsen.com/news-center/2026/streaming-embarks-on-annual-summer-ascent-in-nielsens-may-2026-gauge-reports/)per Nielsen's [Gauge](https://www.nielsen.com/news-center/2026/streaming-embarks-on-annual-summer-ascent-in-nielsens-may-2026-gauge-reports/), though anyone citing a Gauge number this year should know that Nielsen is recalibrating the report against new universe estimates for the coming season, and the post-recalibration shares are expected to read differently.

[OTT](https://www.aidigital.com/blog/what-is-ott-advertising) sits alongside CTV as a description of content delivery, where CTV describes the ad execution.

_💡 AI Digital's guide to_ [_CTV advertising_](https://www.aidigital.com/blog/connected-tv-advertising) _covers buying models and measurement frameworks in full, and the_ [_OTT vs CTV_](https://www.aidigital.com/blog/ott-vs-ctv) _breakdown covers where the two diverge._

## How we verified these results

Every figure on this page was traced back to the organization that produced it: the streaming platform, the DSP, the agency, or the trade publication that reported it first. Each entry names its source and links to it, and where a campaign year has been published it appears alongside the result. Where a platform has never published one, the entry says so.

That standard has visible consequences. Platform-reported figures are labeled as such, since a streaming service publishing its own client's results has an obvious interest in the outcome and readers deserve to weigh the number accordingly. Roku accounts for four of the eight campaigns here, a concentration that comes down to disclosure practice: the company publishes considerably more first-party client case studies than anyone else in the market.

Applying the same standard also removed two campaigns that appear on almost every competing list. Volvo's 35% sales lift from interactive CTV traces to a September 2018 Marketing Dive report of an Innovid study, and it now circulates with its date detached. Subway's 33% sales figure comes from the August 2021 results of the "Eat Fresh Refresh" relaunch, which ran across television, digital, social, in-store, and print, and no source attributes that number to connected TV specifically. Accurate in their original contexts, both have since been recycled into claims their sources never made.

## What makes a successful CTV ad campaign?

Across wildly different budgets, high-performing connected TV campaigns tend to be assembled the same way, with four components carrying most of the weight.

1.  **Creative built for the screen and the remote.** Short-form video designed for TV consistently outperforms repurposed linear spots, and the addition of a remote-activated action changes what the format can do. A clear opening, one explicit call to action, and messaging aligned to funnel stage produce more downstream response than a longer brand film.
2.  **Data beyond age and gender.** Household-level signals, purchase intent, category browsing, and location proximity give CTV

# CTV Dictionary: Your Guide to Connected TV Terms

![what-is-ctv-advertising-definitions](/_next/image?url=%2Fapi%2Ffiles%2FCTV-Dictionary-BhI7ACSHXiMErjbKop31Bw.png&w=3840&q=75)

If you’ve ever searched “what is CTV?” or “what is CTV advertising?” you’re not alone. These terms get thousands of searches every month. (Yes, we did our SEO research. Consider this blog our official answer to the internet.)

As connected TV continues to reshape television advertising, the terminology can feel overwhelming. Between OTT platforms, CTV measurement, ROAS calculations, geo targeting, programmatic media buying, and full funnel marketing, it’s easy to get lost in the acronyms.

This CTV dictionary is your go-to reference guide. Whether you're new to streaming TV ads or refining your CTV advertising strategy, this glossary breaks down the most important terms in clear, practical language.

## CTV (Connected TV)

CTV (Connected TV) refers to any television that connects to the internet and streams video content. This includes:

*   Smart TVs
*   Streaming devices like Roku, Fire TV, or Apple TV
*   Gaming consoles
*   TVs connected to OTT platforms

In short, if a TV is streaming content through the internet, it qualifies as connected TV.

FYI: [CTV viewership](https://adsmanager.paramount.com/insights/report-ctv-advertising-vs-social-ad-performance) now represents a major share of total TV time, making it one of the most important advertising trends in modern media planning.

## CTV Ads

CTV ads are non-skippable video advertisements served within streaming TV content. They typically run for 15 or 30 seconds and appear full-screen.

[Best practices](https://adsmanager.paramount.com/insights/ctv-video-ad-creative-best-practices-holiday-advertising) to make TV ads engaging for streaming viewers:

*   Strong opening hook in the first 3–5 seconds
*   Clear, simple messaging
*   On-screen branding
*   Verbal and visual call-to-action

## CTV Ads Manager

A CTV ad manager is a campaign management advertising platform that allows advertisers to create, launch, and monitor ads across platforms. Typically includes build-in audience targeting and performance reports. Need an example? [Why not try out Paramount Ads Manager >](https://adsmanager.paramount.com/sign-up)

## CTV Ad Measurement

CTV ad measurement refers to tracking and analyzing the performance of streaming campaigns. Common CTV marketing metrics include:

### Brand Lift:

Measures the impact of advertising on awareness, perception, and purchase intent, often used to measure upper funnel impact beyond direct conversions.

### CTV CPMs (Cost per thousand impressions):

The cost to deliver 1,000 impressions with an ad.

Formula: (Total Spend ÷ Impressions) × 1,000

### CPL (Cost per lead):

The cost to generate one qualified lead from an ad.

### Impressions:

The total number of times an ad is served & seen by a viewer.

### ROAS (Return on Ad Spend):

Measures marketing investment ROI (return on investment) based on revenue generated for every dollar spent on advertising.

ROAS calculation formula: Revenue ÷ Ad Spend

### TV Attribution Analysis:

Measurement that connects CTV exposure to downstream actions such as website visits, app download, in-store visits, or purchases.

### VCR (Video Completion Rate):

The percentage of viewers who watch a video ad from start to finish.

Formula: Completed Views ÷ Total Impressions

## CTV Advertising

CTV advertising refers to video ads that run on connected TV devices through streaming services. Unlike traditional television advertising, CTV ads allow for:

*   Household-level targeting (ZIP code, age, gender, income)
*   Real-time campaign measurement and reporting
*   Attribution tracking
*   Retargeting across devices
*   Self-serve campaign creation through online advertising platforms

## CTV Audience Targeting

The ability to deliver ads based on geographic and demographic filters such as ZIP code, age, gender, or income. With CTV ad platforms like Paramount Ads Manager, you can target based on the following:

### Geo-targeting:

A targeting method that delivers ads based on geographic location, including Country, State, DMA (Designated Market Area), ZIP code, or radius targeting around a specific address. This is particularly valuable for local TV advertising and regional businesses.

### Contextual targeting:

[Contextual targeting](https://adsmanager.paramount.com/insights/ctv-contextual-targeting) serves ads based on the content being watched rather than individual user data. For example, running auto ads during sports content.

### Custom Audiences:

Custom audiences allow advertisers to target viewers using their own first-party data, like CRM email lists, website visitors

# How to advertise on CTV

[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=How%20to%20advertise%20on%20CTV%20-%20https://comcastadvertising.com/insights/knowledge-hub/how-to-advertise-on-connected-tv/)[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://comcastadvertising.com/insights/knowledge-hub/how-to-advertise-on-connected-tv/)[](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https://comcastadvertising.com/insights/knowledge-hub/how-to-advertise-on-connected-tv/)

![Two women with mugs sitting on the couch](https://comcastadvertising.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/3-How-to-advertise-on-CTV-.webp)

You’re likely very familiar with connected TV (CTV), content streamed over the internet on the TV screen. With today’s audiences leaning into streaming, and with [most streaming happening on the TV screen](https://comcastadvertising.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/2026_CA_Report.pdf), connected TV is now a core part of how people watch television.

In fact, CTV represents more than a third of total TV viewing,1 so there’s no better time to learn how to advertise on CTV. As streaming grows, CTV advertising gives businesses a powerful way to reach audiences on the biggest screen in the home, even when those audiences are not watching traditional TV.

If you’ve been wondering, “How do I advertise on CTV?” here’s a brief overview to get you started.

## How Does Connected TV Work?

Advertising on CTV follows many of the same foundational steps as [traditional TV advertising](https://comcastadvertising.com/insights/knowledge-hub/how-to-advertise-on-tv/). Understanding these steps helps businesses plan campaigns that are effective, efficient, and aligned with their goals.

Follow the outline below to plan and launch your successful CTV advertising campaign.

### 1\. Define Your Target Audience

Success in CTV advertising starts with knowing who you want to reach. The more detailed the description, the better. You can define audiences using a combination of geography, household characteristics, viewing trends, and interests. This allows you to move beyond broad demographics and deliver ads to households that are more likely to be in the market for your products or services.

### 2\. Decide Your Budget

Connected TV advertising costs vary based on targeting, market size, ad length, and demand, but CTV advertisers typically pay based on impressions delivered to their desired audience.

### 3\. Produce Your CTV Ad

CTV ads typically look like traditional TV commercials, most commonly 15- or 30-second video spots, but they are served in streaming environments with fewer ad breaks. This means each ad often receives more focused attention.

Make the most of the opportunity by delivering a clear message with strong visuals and a compelling call to action. Keep in mind that connected TV advertising allows you to do more than linear TV commercials because viewers may be able to interact with your ad or even take immediate action through their TV. If concepting and producing video is outside your comfort zone, many advertising partners offer [creative services](https://comcastadvertising.com/advertising/client-creative/).

### 4\. Purchase the CTV Advertising Space

CTV buying focuses on reaching defined audiences across streaming content, regardless of the exact program those audiences are tuned into. There are two main ways to buy that access:

*   Use a full-service agency that will handle everything for you.
*   Use a platform that facilitates doing it on your own.

With a fully managed approach, your campaigns are put together by experts in marketing strategy, audience identification, inventory access, optimization, and reporting.

The DIY method can use a variety of self-serve platforms that may be more budget friendly. These tools empower advertisers to secure placements in high
